recent_posts.title: Progress Report: Linux 7.0
recent_posts.summary: Asahi Linux's progress report coinciding with Linux 7.0 covers several major developments: the Asahi Installer has been updated to v0.8.0 with CI/CD automation via GitHub Actions, ending two years of manual releases. Ambient light sensor (ALS) support is now available via Apple's Always-On Processor with a firmware update workflow. Power Management Processor (PMP) driver support saves ~0.5W idle power on M1 Pro machines. Bluetooth coexistence fixes eliminate audio dropouts. Variable Refresh Rate (VRR) support was discovered hidden in a DCP firmware parameter and is available via a kernel module flag. Audio improvements include new sample rate support (44.1, 88.2, 176.4, 192 kHz) for the headphone jack chip and upstream merging of bus keeper APIs. M3 machines now have PCIe, keyboard, trackpad, NVMe, and RTC support. Fedora Asahi Remix 44 is on track for release with KDE Plasma 6.6 features.

recent_posts.title: Progress Report: Linux 6.19
recent_posts.summary: Asahi Linux's progress report for Linux 6.19 covers several major milestones. DisplayPort Alt Mode via USB-C is now working in the experimental 'fairydust' branch after years of reverse engineering four hardware blocks (DCP, DPXBAR, ATCPHY, ACE), though it remains developer-only due to known quirks. M3 MacBook Air can now boot to a full Plasma desktop thanks to three new contributors, but a general release requires GPU driver work, DCP bring-up, and speaker safety support. 14"/16" MacBook Pros now support 120 Hz displays starting with kernel 6.18.4. The DCP driver is being refactored to support hardware planes, HDR experiments, Y'CbCr video, and a new 'Apple Interchange' compressed framebuffer format. Webcam support was fixed across multiple layers including Mesa, PipeWire, and the GPU kernel driver. GPU upstreaming has begun with IGT test patches, and OpenGL/Vulkan memory copy and clear performance saw major improvements. Fedora Asahi Remix is also gaining a DNF5-based PackageKit backend.

recent_posts.title: Progress Report: Linux 6.18
recent_posts.summary: Linux 6.18 brings significant progress for Apple Silicon support through the Asahi Linux project. Key achievements include merging SMC subdevice drivers (hwmon and RTC) for 6.19, upstreaming USB3 support via USB-C ports, and fixing microphone support on M2 Pro/Max MacBooks (resolved by correcting a single DMA range property). The team is improving the installation experience by working with Anaconda and KDE Plasma Setup to enable safer, more flexible installations directly from live media without risking Apple's critical system partitions. An Asahi-themed talk is scheduled for 39C3.

recent_posts.title: Progress Report: Linux 6.17
recent_posts.summary: Linux 6.17 brings significant progress for Apple Silicon support, including the long-awaited SMC core driver merge and GPU devicetree groundwork. The m1n1 bootloader is transitioning to Rust for safety-critical components, while 64-bit Windows games now run via WINE outside muvm. New developer tools like tuxvdmtool enable Linux-based development workflows, and geometry shader emulation work benefits other mobile GPU drivers. Basic M3 support exists at the bootloader level, with Fedora Asahi Remix 43 dailies now available.

recent_posts.title: Progress Report: Linux 6.16
recent_posts.summary: Linux 6.16 brings significant improvements to Asahi Linux for Apple Silicon Macs. The Mesa GPU drivers are now fully upstream, eliminating the need for custom Flatpak extensions and completing the transition to upstream graphics stack. Performance optimizations in Mesa 25.2 provide notable improvements, especially for gaming. A new WoW64 implementation allows 32-bit Windows applications to run without virtualization, improving performance and reducing complexity. The project has upstreamed over 200 patches, reducing downstream maintenance burden by 20%. Additional improvements include SPMI controller support, audio driver updates, and various bug fixes for Plymouth and OBS screencasting.

recent_posts.title: Progress Report: Linux 6.15
recent_posts.summary: Linux 6.15 introduces key advancements such as the merging of the graphics driver uAPI into the kernel, enabling support for Apple Silicon devices in upstream Mesa. Fedora Asahi Remix 42 has been released, offering an updated experience for users. The report also highlights the upstreaming of kernel patches for Apple SoCs, infrastructure improvements, and new guidelines for distro support. Upcoming efforts include more driver updates for Linux 6.16.

recent_posts.title: Progress Report: Linux 6.14
recent_posts.summary: The Asahi Linux team provides a progress update as Linux 6.14 nears release. They've focused on upstream patch submissions and reducing downstream patches, with new drivers submitted and accepted. Microphone support has been enabled on most laptops, and Fedora Asahi Remix 42 Beta is available. The team also enabled Bluetooth device synchronization across macOS installs and received significant financial support from the community, which aids in future sustainability and development.

recent_posts.title: Passing the torch on Asahi Linux
recent_posts.summary: Asahi Linux founder Hector Martin (marcan) has resigned, leading to changes in the project's governance and funding. A new team will share leadership responsibilities, and Open Source Collective will now facilitate donations. Future priorities include kernel upstreaming and continuous integration testing. New features expected in 2025 include DP alt mode, sparse images in the Vulkan driver, and internal microphone support on select Apple Silicon devices.

recent_posts.title: Beyond Gaming: X11 bridging in muvm
recent_posts.summary: Asahi Linux has introduced an update to its x86/x86-64 emulation stack, facilitating the use of non-game applications with native performance in VMs through DRM Native Context. Unlike traditional GPU passthrough methods, this approach effectively splits the GPU driver stack between the host and the guest. The update also introduces muvm-x11bridge for X11 passthrough, replacing the less efficient sommelier. Despite some initial challenges with synchronization and futexes, these updates significantly enhance the performance and usability of non-game apps on Asahi Linux's virtualized environment.

recent_posts.title: AAA gaming on Asahi Linux
recent_posts.summary: Asahi Linux has introduced a toolkit that enables AAA gaming on M1 and M2 Apple hardware, integrating Vulkan 1.3 drivers with x86 emulation and Windows compatibility. The setup involves installing Fedora Asahi Remix and setting up specific drivers. While the current release is in alpha, it supports games like Control, Fallout 4, and Cyberpunk 2077, though demanding titles may require 16GB of RAM. Future updates aim to enhance performance and compatibility with more games.
